Operator
Good day, everyone. My name is Ryan, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I'd like
to welcome you all to the Ameren Corporation Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] At
this time, I'd like to turn the call over to Andrew Kirk, Senior Director of Investor Relations and Corporate
Modeling.
Andrew Kirk
Senior Director of Investor Relations & Corporate Modeling
Thank you, and good morning. On the call with me today are Marty Lyons, Chairman, President and Chief
Executive Officer; Michael Moehn, Group President of our Ameren Utilities; and Lenny Singh, Executive
Vice President and Chief Financial Officer; as well as other members of the Ameren management team.

This call contains time-sensitive data that is accurate only as of the date of today's live broadcast, and
redistribution of this broadcast is prohibited. We have posted a presentation on the amereninvestors.com
homepage that will be referenced by our speakers. As noted on Page 2 of the presentation, comments
made during this conference call may contain statements about future expectations, plans, projections,
financial performance and similar matters, which are commonly referred to as forward-looking statements.

Please refer to the forward-looking statements section in the news release we issued yesterday as well
as our SEC filings for more information about the various factors that could cause actual results to differ
materially from those anticipated.

Lastly, all per share earnings amounts discussed during today's presentation, including earnings guidance,
are presented on a diluted basis, unless otherwise noted.

Now here's Marty, who will start on Page 4.
Martin J. Lyons
President, CEO & Chairman of the Board
Thanks, Andrew. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Starting on Page 4 with key
highlights. Today, we're very excited to share an update to our growth story, one driven by growing
customer energy needs, economic development across our region and the need for an even more resilient
grid. We are well positioned to meet these needs, support expansion and deliver durable value to our
customers, communities and shareholders.

First, reflecting our strong year-to-date performance and outlook, we have raised our 2026 earnings
per share guidance range and issued 2027 earnings per share guidance that represents solid year-over-
year growth. Looking further ahead, we have also raised our long-term growth outlook with expected
compound annual earnings per share growth of 8% to 10% from 2027 through 2031. This outlook reflects
strong economic development across our service territory, particularly in Missouri, where 2.8 gigawatts of
signed electric service agreements underpin our higher sales forecast and increased generation investment
plan with additional opportunities in the pipeline.

Regional economic growth is also driving incremental investment opportunities in our Transmission
segment to connect new generation resources and serve new large load customers. To meet this
increasing energy need, we plan to strategically invest $38.1 billion in energy infrastructure over the next
5 years, which is expected to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from 2026 through 2031.
What excites me most about this plan is the opportunity to create lasting value for our customers and
communities through a safer, more reliable and more resilient grid while directly supporting a growing
economy with more and better jobs.

Indeed, our strategy, outlined on Page 5, is centered on delivering value to the customers and
communities we serve, including 2.5 million electric and 900,000 natural gas customers across Missouri

and Illinois. By investing in and strengthening our energy infrastructure, advocating for constructive
energy policies and continuously optimizing performance to improve service quality, we are delivering on
what matters most to our customers, safe, reliable energy at the lowest cost possible.

Turning to Page 6. Execution of our strategy is delivering tangible customer benefits. Over time, we have
achieved top quartile reliability performance and strong customer service satisfaction. We have also
supported tens of billions of dollars in annual economic impact and in 2025 alone, an estimated 63,000
jobs while keeping average residential rates below national and Midwest averages. And that's before
factoring in the significant additional economic impact from the large load and other customer growth our
investments facilitate, including significant incremental tax revenue for our communities.
Highlighted on Page 7, execution of our strategy has also delivered strong, consistent shareholder results.
Since divesting our merchant business in 2013, weather-normalized adjusted earnings per share have
grown at a compound annual rate of approximately 7.4%, annual dividends per share have increased
78% and total shareholder return has exceeded 300%, significantly outperforming utility index averages.
Looking ahead, we believe continued execution of this strategy, centered on delivering value for customers
and communities will continue to drive superior long-term returns for our shareholders.

Turning now to Page 8. Here, we reiterate our strategic priorities for 2026. Targeted, timely infrastructure
investments are key to delivering reliable service. As shown on the right, we invested more than $4
billion in energy infrastructure through September to strengthen reliability and resiliency and improve
service. The value of continued investment was evident during the third quarter's extreme heat when
our infrastructure performed well and our team successfully managed the system through periods of
exceptionally high demand, keeping our coworkers safe, homes cool and businesses running.

This year's severe weather, with Illinois leading the nation in tornado activity, further underscores the
importance of building a stronger, more resilient energy system and having skilled teams in place to
operate it safely and reliably. In 2026, through September, investments in grid automation helped avoid
more than 63 million customer outage minutes across both Missouri and Illinois, a tangible example of
how infrastructure investment translates into better service. We also made strong progress on many other
objectives, which I'll discuss in a moment.

Moving to Page 9. Yesterday, we reported third quarter 2026 earnings of $2.42 per share compared to
adjusted earnings of $2.17 per share in the third quarter of 2025. The key drivers of our strong third
quarter results are outlined on this page. In light of a strong year-to-date performance, we raised our
2026 earnings per share guidance range to $5.35 to $5.55 from our original range of $5.25 to $5.45.

Turning to Page 10 for our 2027 guidance outlook. We have a long track record of strong and consistent
earnings per share growth. As we look ahead, we expect this to continue. We expect 2027 earnings to be
in the range of $5.70 to $5.90 per share. The midpoint of this range represents 8.4% earnings per share
growth compared to our original 2026 earnings guidance midpoint. Lenny will provide the key drivers for
2026 and expected 2027 earnings later in the call.

Turning to Page 11 and Ameren Missouri sales growth expectations. At Ameren, we are proud to provide
the quality of service that is necessary to attract investment and economic growth to our region. The
pipeline of economic development interest within our service territory remains robust across Missouri
and Illinois. Our 5-year financial plan laid out today assumes 12.9% compound annual sales growth in
Missouri from 2027 through 2031 based on an assumption of 2.9 gigawatts of new load by 2031. This
growth assumption, as depicted by the dashed green line on the chart on the right-hand side of this page,
is consistent with our preferred resource plan through 2030, which projects a 60% increase in Missouri
sales by 2030 from 2027 levels. This growth is supported by the existing 2.8 gigawatts of electric service
agreements with sales from those agreements expected to reach full capacity in 2030.

Beyond these signed agreements, our pipeline includes 1.2 gigawatts of projects with construction
agreements and an additional 4.4 gigawatts of projects with completed interconnection studies. We were
pleased to see one of the projects with a completed interconnection study advance to a construction
agreement since our second quarter update. Consistent with the requirements of Missouri Senate Bill 4,
large load customers will pay for the power and infrastructure costs driven by their operations. And once

their sites are operational, large load customers will contribute to paying fixed costs of the energy grid,
providing long-term cost benefits for other customers.

Moving then to Page 12 for an update on Missouri's generation plan. In September, Ameren Missouri filed
its 2026 Integrated Resource Plan, updating its 20-year road map to reliably and cost effectively meet
customers' energy needs under a range of future conditions. Using an optimal mix of natural gas, solar,
energy storage, wind, nuclear and other technologies, our preferred resource plan is designed to serve 3.4
gigawatts of additional demand by 2031 and 5 gigawatts by 2036. To support this growth, the plan calls
for accelerating and expanding natural gas generation and battery storage, expanding solar generation
and adding fuel cell generation, extending the retirement date of 2 Labadie Energy Center units from 2036
to 2042 and adding new nuclear generation by 2040.
Importantly, the table on this page identifies the preferred resource plan additions included in our 2027
through 2031 capital plan. The 5-year capital plan supports 2.9 gigawatts of incremental load growth
by 2031. Preferred plan resources identified as not included in our 5-year capital and rate base growth
plans represent potential upside to our outlook as we execute additional electric service agreements. We
will continue to provide updates on any additional electric service agreements and associated investment
needs as appropriate.

On Page 13, we outline how continued execution of our strategy is expected to drive strong growth over
the next 5 years. Today, we're rolling forward our 5-year capital plan, which now totals $38.1 billion,
reflecting significant investment to serve the anticipated load growth I just discussed while strengthening
system reliability. We expect these investments to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from
2026 through 2031. Leveraging our proven strategy and building upon our track record of strong earnings
growth, we expect to deliver 8% to 10% compound annual earnings per share growth from 2027 through
2031, using our 2027 guidance midpoint of $5.80 per share as the base.

As large load sales ramp in 2028 and 2029, we expect annual earnings per share growth near the upper
end of that range in those years. We also expect to deliver strong, sustainable annual dividend growth as
our earnings grow with a payout ratio ranging between 45% to 55%. As we invest to support meaningful
economic growth in our communities, our focus remains on delivering reliable, affordable service for all
customers with large load customers paying the cost required to serve their operations. I'm truly excited
about the opportunity to support this significant growth and the lasting benefits it can bring to local
communities and across our region.

I'll now turn the call over to Michael to discuss our disciplined approach to delivering the generation and
transmission resources needed to meet our growing sales.
Michael L. Moehn
Group President, Ameren Utilities
Thanks, Marty, and good morning, everyone. I'll begin on Page 15. As Marty outlined, significant economic
development is driving growing energy needs across our region. Our economic development teams
remain focused on supporting long-term business investment and job growth. That work is translating
into tangible results for our communities. During the second quarter, Google and Amazon announced
projects in our Missouri service territory, representing a combined planned investment of $25 billion.
These projects are part of the 2.8 gigawatts of ESAs we signed earlier this year.

As you can see from the photos on this page, the projects are well underway. These projects are creating
thousands of construction jobs for local contractors and small businesses and will directly employ
hundreds of people longer term once operational. These projects are also expected to generate billions
of dollars in local tax revenue, helping fund schools and public safety, including fire stations and police
stations, and improve roads, delivering lasting benefits to the communities where they operate. Beyond
these investments, Google and Amazon have committed millions of dollars through community benefit
agreements to support new workforce development, energy efficiency and community-focused programs,
both locally and across Missouri. We will continue to work closely with businesses interested in locating
operations in our service territory to find the right solutions to meet their energy needs and ultimately
support economic development in the region.

Moving to Page 16. We continue to make strong progress advancing our generation portfolio to support
customers' growing energy needs with a focus on reliability and affordability. As our generation investment
grows, we are applying lessons learned across projects through a disciplined portfolio-based execution
model. This includes standardizing designs and equipment as appropriate, securing long lead components
early, leveraging experienced engineering and construction partners across multiple projects and
strengthening our internal team to provide consistent oversight.

Work underway at the Castle Bluff and Big Hollow Energy Centers is helping establish a repeatable
execution model for other projects, including the 2.1 gigawatt West Alton Energy Center. This approach
is designed to improve productivity, better coordinate resources across projects and increase schedule
and cost predictability. We believe this approach positions us well to effectively execute future generation
projects and meet increasing customer demand.

Turning to Page 17. The execution focus we just discussed is critical as we advance Ameren Missouri's
broader generation plan. Consistent with our 2026 preferred resource plan, we are developing a balanced
and diverse portfolio that includes adding approximately 7.7 gigawatts of new generation capacity
from 2027 through 2031, which would increase Ameren Missouri's installed capacity by approximately
80%. With 5.3 gigawatts of announced projects, we are making tangible progress towards that target.
Approximately 2.3 gigawatts of simple cycle gas, solar and battery storage resources have received
regulatory approval, are under construction and are expected to begin serving customers in 2027 and
2028.

In July, we filed a CCN request for the 2.1 gigawatt West Alton facility, which is expected to be in service
in 2031. In October, the Missouri PSC approved CCN request for nearly 1 gigawatt of solar and storage
resources following a 5-month review. These projects are expected to begin serving customers in 2028
and 2029. With more than 5 gigawatts of new generation resources in progress and more in the pipeline,
I'm pleased to say that our teams are well positioned to deliver these projects on schedule for our
customers. Planned generation additions are expected to generate approximately $2.75 billion of tax
credits from 2027 through 2031, providing significant savings for our customers.

As new large load electric demand evolves, our focus remains on serving all our customers reliably and
affordably by carefully planning and executing grid upgrades, maintaining a balanced generation portfolio
and ensuring costs to serve new large load customers are appropriately allocated to such customers in
accordance with Senate Bill 4.

Moving to Page 18 for a transmission update. We continue making robust investment in our region's
transmission infrastructure to ensure ongoing reliability and efficiency. We expect our transmission
investment levels to remain strong over time to support new large load customers and to connect the
generation resources required to serve our territory reliably as regional demand grows. At the same time,
we remain focused on executing our assigned and awarded long-range transmission projects for the first 2
MISO LRTP tranches. In the second quarter, MISO selected our joint proposals for the WIIL and STIW LRTP
Tranche 2 competitive projects located in our Illinois service territory.

Notably, we have won the opportunity to develop all 5 competitive long-range transmission projects in
our service territory within both the Tranche 1 and Tranche 2 portfolios, reflecting our strong record of
delivering high-quality transmission infrastructure at a competitive cost. I'm also pleased to say that last
month, our joint proposal for the competitive EASL transmission project located in Iowa was selected from
among multiple bids. Over half of the approximate $500 million investment opportunity is included in the
capital plan issued today. Importantly, this marks our first competitive transmission project award outside
of our service territory and further demonstrates our ability to effectively and efficiently design, build and
operate high-quality transmission infrastructure.

On Page 19, we outlined the investment pipeline across our businesses over the next decade. These
investments will support safety, reliability and resiliency of the energy grid and economic development in
our region, while positioning our system to power the quality of life for all of our customers in our territory.
The pipeline now includes more than $90 billion of investment opportunity through 2036. The $19 billion
increase in our 10-year pipeline primarily reflects the investments needed to serve the 5 gigawatts of load
growth assumed within the new Ameren Missouri Preferred Resource Plan by 2036.

Moving to Page 20. We recognize that our critical infrastructure projects represent significant investments,
which is why we prioritize the projects that are most beneficial for customers and maintain a sharp focus
on keeping rates as low as possible. Through disciplined cost management, we've been able to keep our
Ameren supplied residential rates in Missouri and Illinois on average below both national and Midwest
averages. In addition, Ameren invests hundreds of millions of dollars each year to support our customers
and communities through energy efficiency programs and demand response initiatives. In October,
we announced $10 million of additional funding for programs to help eligible customers in need across
Missouri and Illinois manage their energy bills. In addition to funding Ameren developed programs, we
also partner with a wide range of organizations to connect customers with available federal, state and
local assistance. In 2026, through September, Ameren customers received more than $107 million in total
energy assistance.

We're also focused on affordability through transformational process improvements, including
implementation of several operational process enhancements designed to increase efficiency and help
manage cost. Since implementing these programs, we have achieved savings of over $100 million
annually. For example, we have implemented a standardized planning and scheduling model across
distribution operations that improves how work is planned, prioritized, cost estimated and executed,
reducing costs and enabling crews to be more productive. We've also implemented initiatives designed to
strengthen the efficiency of our third-party spend.

And also underway, we're working to improve the productivity of our gas operations through standardized
operating practices and optimize crew deployment, streamlining operating costs while maintaining strong
safety, service and emergency response performance. We're also advancing a multiyear digital road map
to optimize operating costs, simplify the technology landscape and position the company to leverage
automation and AI capabilities more effectively. I'm excited by the operational milestones achieved to
date, and I'm confident in our team's ability to effectively execute our investment plans in a way that
benefits our customers and communities.

I will now turn the call over to Lenny for a financial update.
Leonard P. Singh
Executive VP & CFO
Thanks, Michael. I'll begin on Page 22 of our presentation. Yesterday, we reported third quarter 2026
GAAP earnings of $2.42 per share compared to third quarter 2025 GAAP earnings of $2.35 per share
and adjusted earnings of $2.17 per share. The difference between 2025 GAAP and the adjusted earnings
reflected a previous disclosure of tax benefit of $0.18 per share. The year-over-year third quarter increase
primarily reflected higher sales and favorable weather, higher earnings on investments in innovative
energy technologies and higher earnings on infrastructure investments to improve system reliability,
resiliency and service quality.

The third quarter was the warmest in St. Louis in more than 50 years with the month of September being
the hottest on record. Separate from the impact of weather, we continue to experience solid customer
growth at Ameren Missouri, where weather-normalized electric retail sales for the trailing 12 months
ended September increased approximately 0.5%, primarily driven by the growth in the commercial
customer class. These positive factors were partially offset by higher operations and maintenance
expenses at Ameren Missouri, primarily driven by increased reliability focused efforts.

Moving to Page 23 for select considerations for the remainder of the year. As Marty noted, yesterday,
we raised our 2026 earnings per share guidance due to strong year-to-date performance. The revised
outlook assumes normal temperatures for the remainder of the year. As we close out the year, we expect
higher expenditures for distribution line inspections, tree trimming and energy center maintenance that
will strengthen service for our customers. Through continued execution of our strategy, we remain focused
on delivering 2026 earnings within our updated guidance range.

Turning to Pages 24 and 25 for a brief update on the Missouri electric rate review we filed with the Missouri
PSC in late June. The review is proceeding according to the established procedural schedule, and we
expect Missouri PSC staff and other intervenors to file direct testimony in early December. Recall the

requested revenue increase is designed to recover the cost of significant system reliability and resiliency
investments. In addition to incorporating meaningful improvements for our customers, this request also
includes $21 million in savings from projected data center revenues for our other retail customers and
establishes a new income-eligible discount rate to supplement our financial assistance programs already
in place. We look forward to working with the Missouri PSC staff and other stakeholders throughout the
review process to achieve a constructive outcome. We expect the Missouri PSC order by May 2027 with
new rates reflecting the approved adjustment effective by June 2027.

Moving to Page 26 for an update on Ameren Illinois regulatory matters. 2025 annual reconciliation
proceeding under the electric multiyear rate plan continues to progress. The $28 million adjustment we
are requesting reflects 2025 actual cost, actual year-end rate base and the allowed return on equity
and common equity ratio established in the multiyear rate plan. Notably, our requested adjustment is
aligned with the ICC staff and administrative law judge's recommendations. An ICC decision is expected in
December with the approved reconciliation adjustment reflected in rates in 2027.

Moving to the Ameren Illinois multiyear grid plan proceeding. We proposed a $2.7 billion electric
distribution investment plan for 2028 through 2031. The plan is designed to strengthen grid safety,
reliability and resiliency while preparing the system to support evolving customer needs and Illinois' clean
energy objectives. Last month, the administrative law judge recommended approval of the grid plan with
proposed downward adjustments to our capital plan of approximately $200 million. We expect an ICC
decision on the proposed investment plan by December. The approved multiyear grid plan will inform a
rate review filing we expect to make in the first quarter of 2027.

Turning to Page 27. We look at our company-wide capital plan for the next 5 years. As Marty highlighted,
we see robust investment opportunities ahead. The plan we are releasing today calls for $38.1 billion in
capital expenditures from 2027 through 2031, an increase of more than 20% compared to our capital
plan issued last year. The increase in our capital plan reflects the roll forward of our plan from 2030 to
2031, the firming up of cost estimates and project timing and the incorporation of new investments.
The investments themselves primarily reflect significant new generation additions at Ameren Missouri,
critical upgrades to strengthen and maintain an aging grid across all operating segments and expanded
transmission investments to execute awarded MISO LRTP competitive projects interconnect new
generation to serve large load customers and support resource adequacy across the region. We expect this
investment to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from 2026 to 2031, which is outlined by
business segment on this page.

Turning to Pages 28 and 29, where we provide a financing update. We continue to feel good about our
financial position. As we fund our robust infrastructure plan, we remain focused on maintaining a strong
balance sheet and strong credit metrics. Our primary source of funding will continue to be cash from
operations, which we expect to increase as sales grow and rates are updated to reflect our investment in
energy infrastructure. Additional funding needs will be financed in a balanced manner, consistent with our
past practices. We fulfilled our 2026 equity needs in 2025, primarily through $600 million of forward sales
agreements that we expect to settle near the end of the year.

We expect to issue approximately $5 billion of equity from 2027 through 2031 and have sold forward in
2026 approximately $1.7 billion of common stock under our at-the-market program to address a portion
of those needs. We've had success utilizing our ATM program and expect to continue to leverage the
program going forward. We appreciate the flexibility our ATM provides, including the ability to effectively
dollar cost average our issuances over time. Based on our anticipated investment and other funding
needs, we expect equity issuances for 2027 through 2031 to be concentrated primarily near year-end
2027 and year-end 2028. Long-term debt will fund remaining cash requirements.

In 2027, we expect approximately $5.2 billion of new long-term issuance to refinance maturing obligations
and fund a portion of our $8.8 billion of planned investments. A portion of such issuances could include
parent company hybrid debt securities, which receive 50% equity credit from Moody's and S&P. Expected
timing for 2027 debt issuances is shown on Page 29. We will continue to proactively manage interest rate
risk associated with planned parent company new issuances through systematic execution of our rate
hedging program. As a reminder, this past spring, S&P and Moody's reaffirmed our stable outlook and BBB

+ and Baa1 credit ratings, respectively. As we've said before, we value our current ratings and remain
committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong credit metrics as we execute our growth plan.

Moving to Page 30 of our presentation. Marty outlined our 2027 earnings per share guidance range earlier.
Expected 2027 earnings detailed by segment compared to our 2026 expectations are highlighted on
this page. Robust planned infrastructure investments, strong expected sales and economic growth and
strategic business process optimization opportunities give us confidence in our ability to deliver strong
earnings growth in 2027 and the years ahead.

In summary, turning to Page 31. We're excited about the opportunities ahead and confident in our
ability to execute our strategic plan and deliver strong, sustainable value to customers, communities
and shareholders. As Marty noted earlier, our outlook includes 8% to 10% compound annual EPS growth
from 2027 through 2031, and we expect EPS growth near the upper end of that range in 2028 and 2029.
This anticipated growth reflects strong economic development with expected 12.9% compound annual
sales growth in Missouri from 2027 through 2031 as well as our $38.1 billion 5-year capital plan that is
expected to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth. Additional electric service agreements and
the infrastructure investments needed to serve that demand represent potential upside to these growth
expectations.

Over the next decade, we have identified an investment pipeline greater than $90 billion needed to
support reliability and anticipated economic growth while delivering meaningful benefits to our customers.
We also expect to deliver strong sustainable annual dividend growth as our earnings grow with a payout
ratio ranging between 45% to 55%. As we execute our robust growth plan, we remain committed to
maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong investment-grade credit ratings.

Taken together, we believe our strong growth outlook, disciplined financing plan, and focus on operational
excellence and execution position us well to deliver long-term value for our customers and competitive
total returns for shareholders.
With that, we'll now open the call for questions.

Question and Answer

Operator
[Operator Instructions] Our first question will come from Shar Pourreza with Wells Fargo.
Andrew Kadavy
Wells Fargo Securities, LLC, Research Division
Actually, it's Andrew Kadavy on for Shar. So looking at the EPS rate CAGR and then also the rate base
CAGR, we've seen a big delta there. The delta has gone up since your last update. Can you talk about
what's driving that? Is it structural? Or is this something that could be narrowed through time?
Martin J. Lyons
President, CEO & Chairman of the Board
Yes. Look, similar to the past, the big delta between the rate base growth and the earnings per share
growth rate that we expect has to do with our financing activities. And as you know, we're going to finance
the capital expenditure plan that we have, the $38.1 billion capital plan, in a very balanced way, consistent
with the way we've historically financed our operations, which means we will be issuing some equity over
time to help with the financing of that. Today, we talked about the fact that we expect about $5 billion of
equity issuances over the next 5 years. We've already got $1.7 billion of that priced through some of the
forward hedging that we've done. But that equity dilution is the primary driver of the difference between
the rate base growth plans that we have and the EPS growth that we expect to be able to deliver over the
next 5 years.
Andrew Kadavy
Wells Fargo Securities, LLC, Research Division
And then moving on to the rate case in Missouri. Are you thinking that you'll be able to settle that case?
Or since it's, kind of, the first one with a large load tariff involved, maybe you want to fully litigate it? And
then on top of that, what kind of outcome are you embedding in your plans for that rate case?
Martin J. Lyons
President, CEO & Chairman of the Board
Yes, I'll start. This is Marty again and see if anybody else wants to chime in. But we're really still in the
very early stages with respect to that rate review. As we indicated in our prepared remarks, this case is
really about infrastructure investments that have been made to serve all of our existing customers. Today,
we really aren't serving any large loads. We expect those sales to begin ramping up in late 2027, and
only modestly in late 2027 and really not ramp up until '28 or '29. So really, this case is really all about
infrastructure investments we've made for our traditional customer base.

We expect, as we mentioned, to see direct testimony from parties in early December. So we haven't seen
any of that yet. However, we do always try to work with the parties in these cases to resolve issues, and
we have a good track record of being able to settle these rate reviews in the past, and that would be our
ambition again as we go into this rate review. So typically, those settlements have occurred sometime
between when true-up testimony is received and the evidentiary hearings begin. So that would signal late
February, early March of next year in terms of a possible, sort of, settlement time frame. And as I sit here
today, again, not having seen any direct testimony yet, but I have no reason to believe we wouldn't be
able to reach agreement with the other parties in the case.
Operator
Our next question will come from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley.
Amanda Huang
Morgan Stanley, Research Division

This is Amanda on for Dave. Maybe the first point on large loads and with ESAs expected to ramp starting
in the second half of '27 and then reaching full capacity in 2030. What are the main items that could
accelerate or delay the ramp? And do you see any impact to earnings from any shift to the expected
ramp?
